Agreed. I will take the suggestion.

What I checked at head: the 2-D tensor default constructor calls `std::construct_at(&data)`, and each row's default constructor is `data()`, so the declaration zero-fills kv_mul x 64 x 4 bytes (4096 bytes at kv_mul 16) [h/tron/tensor/tensor.hpp:40-42, 254-256]. The QK kernel then stores all group_heads rows of all four 16-token blocks before the epilogue reads s_pages [src/tron/kernels/amx_attn.cpp:220-253]. The line itself predates this PR (b431585224). At kv_mul 4 the fill was 1024 bytes. The 16-head shape makes it four times larger, so this PR is the right place to fix it.

On thin LTO: the kernel lives in a separate translation unit, so the fill can only disappear through cross-unit inlining. I did not check whether that happens. With the tag the question does not matter.

Note [Uninitialized Weight Tensors] describes the tag for weight tensors [h/common/util.hpp:289]. This is the first use on a stack scratch buffer, so I will add one line saying why it is safe:

```cpp
      // uninitialized: the QK kernel below writes every element before any read.
      tensor<operation_kv_mul, page::page_size> s_pages{uninitialized};
```

The existing t_amx_numerics and t_amx_dispatch_dtype cases cover this path. The change alters no values.
